title: A fitted monthly residual update cut tidal-range contrast mean squared error by 17% in two US bays in 2011-2025
abstract: We tested whether the previous monthly inland-minus-mouth tidal range improves the next month estimate in Delaware and Chesapeake bays. We used four NOAA gauge snapshots and 178 test months per bay in 2011-2025. Each annual fit used earlier years only. Controls were season, trend and fixed lunar cycles. A fitted lag-one residual update reduced equal-bay mean squared error by 16.68%. Conditional 95% three-year block limits were 9.72% to 21.88%. Root mean squared error fell from 24.05 to 21.95 mm. Delaware and Chesapeake gains were 18.12% and 10.64%. The Chesapeake interval included zero with five-year blocks, and its great-diurnal-range check had no point gain. A full carry-forward update had uncertain pooled gain. The evidence supports a statistical update in this tested scope. It does not identify a physical memory or show real-time skill. Final data, two bays, short records, baseline choices and campaign data reuse limit transfer. Code, a public-domain used-field extract, source hashes, all forecasts, aggregate scores, an internal audit and a figure are included.

display.caption: Annual error reduction and conditional three-year block limits for a fitted one-month residual update in 2011-2025. Positive values favour the update. The pooled score averages bay MSEs before computing the ratio.

citations.reason: Published prior evidence set the lag-update test and its deterministic controls. Data and research context overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
